job.title: Chief Operating Officer
job.description:
The Residential Tenancies Authority (RTA) is a statutory body dedicated to making the renting system work for Queensland. At a time of growth, complexity and heightened expectations across the rental sector, they are seeking an exceptional leader to join the Executive Leadership Team as Chief Operating Officer.

This pivotal role leads a diverse and influential portfolio spanning enterprise change and performance, finance, governance, risk and assurance, legal services, and regulatory compliance and enforcement. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, you will provide trusted advice to the Board and Executive Leadership Team, bringing an enterprise-wide perspective to risk and financial management, organisational performance, decision-making and change management. You will play an important role in translating strategy into action, strengthening organisational capability and ensuring the RTA continues to operate as a contemporary, effective service provider and trusted regulator.

As a key driver of organisational performance and culture, you will lead across multiple specialist functions, bringing people together around shared priorities and creating the conditions for high-performance partnerships and outcomes. Success will require an experienced executive with strong financial and commercial acumen who can promote organisational resilience, build effective risk management capability, and embed governance and enterprise change practices to support the business to achieve its strategic objectives. You will have deep experience drawing on the expertise of specialist teams while maintaining clear executive accountability, balancing strong governance and sound judgement with a pragmatic, values-driven approach to continuous improvement.

The successful candidate will be an accomplished leader who leads with integrity and is comfortable navigating complexity and ambiguity, leading change and building high-performing teams. You will bring extensive experience advising Boards, executives and diverse stakeholders on complex and sensitive matters, together with a strong record of influencing across an organisation, building trust and delivering results. Experience within government, a statutory body, regulated environment or similarly complex organisation or sector will be highly regarded.

The RTA offers the opportunity to influence the future of Queensland’s rental sector, working with a clear mandate to improve performance, strengthen capability, and build confidence, stability and trust in Queensland’s rental system from the start of a new four-year strategic phase. This is a unique opportunity for a senior executive to lead within a values-driven organisation committed to inclusion, collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement.

For more information please contact Gemma Ledbury at 0423 322 462 or email directly to gemmaledbury@attunedtalent.com.au

job.title: HR Projects Coordinator
job.description:
Working within the People team, this role will provide hands-on project coordination, governance and implementation support across a portfolio of enterprise-wide people initiatives. You will work closely with senior HR and change professionals while engaging with stakeholders across a diverse workforce operating in a complex, 24/7 environment.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys bringing structure to projects, coordinating multiple workstreams and contributing to meaningful HR, organisational development and change initiatives, while making a tangible impact over a 12-month contract period.

The opportunity

As the HR Projects Coordinator, you will support the planning, coordination and delivery of strategic People projects spanning organisational capability, performance, culture, engagement, change and broader organisational effectiveness.

You will play an important role in keeping projects moving by coordinating documentation, timelines, governance, reporting and stakeholder engagement. The position will work collaboratively across the People function as well as with leaders, internal teams, external advisors and suppliers.

About you

You will be a highly organised and proactive HR professional or project coordinator who enjoys working across multiple projects and stakeholders. You will bring strong attention to detail alongside the confidence to build relationships, coordinate competing priorities and ensure projects are supported by effective governance and documentation.

Ideally, you will bring:
 
  • Strong HR project coordination skills with experience across project documentation, governance, reporting and tracking.
  • An understanding of HR and People practices and an interest in organisational development, change, transformation or employee engagement.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to work across different functions and levels of an organisation.
  • Excellent organisation and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

If you have a strong foundation in HR and project coordination and are looking for an opportunity where you can contribute to meaningful, enterprise-wide People initiatives, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Commercial Merchandise Manager
job.description:
Blue Bungalow has built a successful business by knowing their customer, choosing product she loves and being prepared to move quickly when they see an opportunity.

They’re an established Australian fashion and lifestyle brand with a loyal customer following and ambitious plans for continued growth. While the business has grown, they’ve remained entrepreneurial, hands-on and close to their customer. They also want to keep it that way.

We’re looking for a Senior Commercial Merchandise Manager to lead their buying team and take ownership of the commercial performance of the merchandise function. Working closely with the Founder, Creative Merchandise Manager and Financial Controller, you’ll bring a strong commercial view to the way they buy. You’ll help determine where they invest, how much they invest and when they need to change course, while leading a team that knows their product and customer incredibly well.

The role
Leading the buying team, the Senior Commercial Merchandise Manager will set clear direction around investment, inventory and performance, with ownership of open-to-buy, merchandise budgets, cash flow and inventory health.

This means staying close to sales and stock performance, understanding where there is an opportunity to invest more and recognising when it’s time to pull back. With product sourced through wholesale, production orders and our own direct development, there is also an important balance to strike between margin opportunity, inventory and cash.

The role works closely with the Creative Merchandise Manager, bringing commercial insight to product decisions while recognising the importance of customer knowledge and creative instinct. It is also an important link into Finance, providing a clear and trusted view of merchandise performance and investment.

Just as importantly, this person will lead and develop the buying team, creating clear accountability and building strong commercial capability across the function.

About you
Your background is likely to be in merchandise planning, merchandise management or commercial buying within fashion, retail or apparel.

Strong capability across open-to-buy, inventory investment, forecasting, margin, stock turn and cash is important, alongside the judgement to know what the numbers mean and what action to take.

You’ll be a confident leader, comfortable setting direction, challenging thinking and making decisions, while giving experienced people the space to do their jobs well.

Blue Bungalow is founder-led, fast-moving and collaborative. We’re looking for someone who enjoys that environment, can operate comfortably at both a strategic and hands-on level, and understands the balance between commercial discipline and great retail instinct.

Why Blue Bungalow?
This is an opportunity to have genuine influence in a successful Australian business as it enters its next stage of growth.

They want to strengthen the commercial capability behind their merchandise decisions while retaining the pace, creativity and understanding of their customer that have made Blue Bungalow what it is today.

job.title: HR Business Partner
job.description:
This is an exciting opportunity to join a fast-growing, highly commercial organisation as a HR Business Partner supporting a commercial and corporate team. Working as part of a collaborative People & Culture team, you will play a key role in delivering commercially focused HR solutions, leading continuous improvement initiatives and driving meaningful people projects that enhance capability, performance and employee experience.

About the role
Reporting to the Head of People Business Partnering, you will partner across a diverse portfolio and provide expert HR support across a broad range of people matters.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Partnering with leaders to deliver strategic and operational HR support across assigned business areas
  • Managing complex ER and IR matters in collaboration with Centres of Excellence
  • Leading and delivering HR projects, transformation initiatives and continuous improvement activities
  • Identifying opportunities to improve HR processes, systems and service delivery
  • Acting as a trusted advisor to leaders, providing commercially focused people solutions
  • Supporting HR Advisors through mentoring, coaching and escalation support; and
  • Using people data and insights to inform decision-making and drive business outcomes

About you
You are an experienced HR professional who enjoys balancing strategic partnering with hands-on delivery. You thrive in fast-paced environments, are comfortable managing competing priorities and enjoy building strong relationships across all levels of a business.

You will bring:
  • 4–5+ years’ experience in a HR generalist, ER/IR or change/project-focused role
  • Strong experience managing complex employee relations matters
  • The ability to influence and engage stakeholders across all levels
  • Strong commercial acumen and a solutions-focused approach
  • Experience leading projects, driving change and improving people processes
  • Relevant qualifications in HR, Business, Law or a related discipline
  • Experience within a fast-paced, complex environment will be highly regarded

Why Apply?

This is an opportunity to join a business with a strong growth trajectory and a high-performance culture where you can make a genuine impact. You will be given the opportunity to contribute across both BAU and strategic initiatives, develop your career and work alongside a supportive and capable People & Culture team.

If you are looking for a role where you can influence, partner, drive change and continue to grow your HR career, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Structural Engineer
job.description:
At Juma Consulting Engineers, they’re passionate about helping bring residential and commercial projects to life through quality pre-construction solutions. As a Brisbane-based business with more than 20 years of industry experience, their team delivers integrated services across building design, structural engineering, soil testing and energy efficiency, supporting projects from concept through to construction with practical expertise and a customer-first mindset.

They are now looking for an experienced Structural Engineer to join the team and take ownership of the commercial and light industrial segment of the business.

This is a hands-on technical opportunity for an engineer who genuinely enjoys the technical aspect and wants to remain close to the design and delivery of projects. While the primary focus will be commercial and light industrial work, there is plenty of variety across the broader business and the opportunity to become involved in more complex residential projects.

The Opportunity

Working closely with the Engineering Manager and broader technical team, you will take responsibility for the structural engineering and delivery of commercial and light industrial projects, with a significant proportion of the current portfolio comprising childcare centres and small warehouse developments.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Lead the structural engineering and design delivery of commercial and light industrial projects
  • Manage projects across childcare centres, warehouses and other small-to-medium commercial developments
  • Undertake structural design across timber-frame, concrete and structural steel construction
  • Design and provide technical input across elements including tilt-up concrete panels, suspended slabs and steel structures
  • Independently manage technical deliverables and sign off engineering work as an RPEQ
  • Work collaboratively with clients, builders, designers and other project stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle
  • Provide practical engineering solutions that balance technical requirements with buildability and commercial considerations
  • Contribute to high-end and multi-storey residential projects where required
  • Build strong, trusted relationships with existing clients and provide a responsive, solutions-focused service
  • Where appropriate, identify opportunities to strengthen existing relationships and contribute to new client and business development opportunities

As an RPEQ, you will have the capability and confidence to take ownership of your work and sign off your own projects.

About You
You are first and foremost a technical Structural Engineer who enjoys getting into the detail, solving engineering problems and delivering high-quality work. You are comfortable taking ownership of projects and enjoy working within a smaller business where you can remain hands-on and have genuine visibility over the outcomes you deliver.
You will ideally bring:
  • RPEQ registration, with the ability to independently sign off structural engineering work
  • Demonstrated structural engineering experience across commercial, light industrial and/or complex residential projects
  • Strong technical capability across timber-frame construction
  • Experience designing concrete structures, including exposure to tilt-up panels and suspended slabs
  • Strong understanding and experience across structural steel
  • The ability to independently manage projects from design through to delivery
  • A practical and solutions-focused approach to engineering and problem solving
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to confidently manage client and stakeholder relationships
  • A willingness to remain hands-on with technical engineering work rather than moving exclusively into people or project management
  • An interest in developing client relationships and, ideally, contributing to the growth of the commercial and light industrial portfolio

job.title: HR Director
job.description:
Join the Fun!
With over 25 years as one of Australia’s leading retailers, EB Games is more than a retail business - it is a brand built on passion, energy and connection. With approximately 300 stores nationally and a workforce of ~3,000 employees, the organisation continues to evolve while staying true to its mission: to run the best pop culture and gaming stores in the world, powered by the most talented retailers.
From its Store Support Centre in Brisbane through to its national retail and operations network, EB Games has created a workplace that balances professionalism with fun - underpinned by strong values, investment in people and a commitment to delivering exceptional customer experiences.
Executive Leadership with Purpose
Reporting to the Managing Director and sitting on the Executive (Director) Team, this is a true executive leadership role, working in partnership with senior leaders to govern the organisation, drive a highly engaged, high-performing and inclusive workforce, and deliver sustained financial success.
You will lead a well-established and highly capable People & Culture function spanning employee and industrial relations, payroll, training and development, HR operations, wellbeing and safety. With strong foundations already in place, the focus of this role is to lead, elevate and enable - aligning people strategy to the organisation’s mission, values and commercial priorities.
Importantly, this role extends beyond functional leadership. As a member of the Director team, you will contribute to broader business governance, including areas such as risk, policy, operations, strategy, budgeting and organisational capability.
Inspire Performance. Shape Culture. Lead Change.
EB Games is a business that values clarity, accountability and momentum. Leaders are empowered, supported and expected to deliver - within an environment that is transparent, structured and aligned to clear strategic priorities.
This role will see you act as an inspirational change leader, creating and casting vision, setting the cultural tone of the organisation and championing a high-performance, inclusive and engaging workplace.
Key areas of focus will include:
  • Strategic alignment: Partnering with the executive team to align people strategy to business goals and sustained financial success
  • Organisational capability: Building leadership, capability and development pathways that support a high-performing workforce
  • Employee & industrial relations: Leading compliant, pragmatic and effective ER/IR practices while coaching leaders through complexity
  • Culture, engagement & wellbeing: Fostering an inclusive, safe and rewarding environment across diverse workforce groups
  • Governance & risk: Contributing to broader organisational governance including policy, compliance, risk and operational effectiveness
  • Transformation & change: Driving initiatives that support growth, evolution and ongoing business improvement

This opportunity will suit a senior HR leader who brings deep expertise across ER/IR, payroll and safety, alongside demonstrated experience leading People & Culture functions within large, multi-site organisations. You will be a decisive and values-led leader, comfortable operating at executive level, with the ability to influence, challenge and inspire.
A competitive package is on offering, including vehicle lease, STI and LTI eligibility and parking on site.  EB Games work a 4:1 hybrid roster and value flexibility.

job.title: Executive Director, Aged Care
job.description:
The future of aged care is changing, and this is an opportunity to lead that change. Lutheran Services is seeking an outstanding executive to lead the transformation of its aged care portfolio, with the immediate priority of building, commercialising and scaling its Support at Home business. As one of Queensland's most respected not-for-profit providers, Lutheran Services is investing in a future-focused operating model that will deliver sustainable growth, exceptional client outcomes and long-term success under Australia's aged care reforms.

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, you will lead a significant portfolio spanning Residential Aged Care, Retirement Living and Support at Home. Your primary focus will be designing and executing a commercially sustainable growth strategy for Support at Home - optimising operating models, improving utilisation, strengthening financial performance and building the capability required to rapidly scale services in an increasingly competitive market. While maintaining oversight of the broader portfolio, success in this role will be defined by your ability to establish Support at Home as a high-performing, growth-focused business.

You are an executive who has successfully built, transformed or scaled community-based health, aged care or human services businesses. You combine strong commercial acumen with operational excellence and understand how to create sustainable growth through innovation, customer experience, workforce optimisation and disciplined financial management. You thrive in complex environments, lead with authenticity and bring the strategic capability to translate reform into commercial opportunity. Experience leading Support at Home, Home Care or community-based services will be highly regarded.

If you are energised by the opportunity to shape the future of care at home and leave a lasting legacy within one of Queensland's leading purpose-driven organisations, we would welcome a confidential discussion.

job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
An opportunity exists for a Financial Controller to join a fast-growing, consumer-led business operating across e-commerce and retail channels. Working closely with the CEO, this role will take ownership of the finance function while bringing greater clarity, structure and insight to a scaling business.

You will establish a clear single source of truth across financial and operational performance, developing reporting, dashboards and insights that enable better decision-making. This includes providing visibility on key metrics such as revenue, margin, inventory and cash flow, as well as identifying trends and drivers of performance to support forward-looking decisions.

This is a hands-on and commercially focused role, suited to someone who can move between detail and strategy. You will contribute to forecasting, modelling and business planning, while partnering across the organisation to support commercial outcomes. A focus on process improvement will be key, including enhancing systems, automating reporting and building scalable financial foundations.

You will bring experience in a senior finance role within a growing business, ideally in e-commerce, retail or a consumer environment. You are technically strong, but equally able to communicate insights clearly and tell the story behind the numbers.

This is an opportunity to play a key role in shaping the finance function within a dynamic business and have a genuine impact on its next phase of growth.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
This is a rare opportunity to lead one of Queensland’s most influential regional organisations and play a central role in shaping the future of the Darling Downs and Surat Basin.

Toowoomba and Surat Basin Enterprise (TSBE) are a respected, member-led organisation that sits at the intersection of business, government and community. Through advocacy, collaboration and strategic leadership, TSBE champions economic growth, investment and opportunity across one of Australia’s most dynamic regional economies.

At a defining moment in the evolution of TSBE, this an opportunity for a new Chief Executive Officer to guide the organisation through its next phase of maturity, influence and impact.

Reporting to the Chair and Board, the CEO will provide strategic leadership across the organisation while serving as its principal advocate and public voice. The role brings together strategy, advocacy and commercial stewardship, ensuring TSBE remains financially sustainable, highly relevant to its members, and an influential voice in regional economic development.

The CEO will build trusted relationships with industry leaders, government stakeholders and regional partners while representing TSBE in critical conversations shaping the region’s future. You will lead organisational performance, strengthen membership and sponsorship engagement, and position TSBE as Australia’s leading regional development organisation.

We are seeking an engaging and outward-facing leader who brings credibility, influence and strong commercial judgement. You will be comfortable operating in complex stakeholder environments and confident advocating for regional priorities with senior decision-makers across government and industry.

This role will suit an experienced executive who is motivated by impact and the opportunity to shape the long-term prosperity of regional Queensland.

For a confidential discussion or to request further information, please contact Gemma Ledbury at gemmaledbury@attunedtalent.com.au

job.title: Regional Chief Financial Officer
job.description:
Brisbane | Executive Leadership | Transform. Influence. Deliver.

This is far more than a traditional CFO role.

Entain ANZ is seeking an exceptional commercial finance executive to partner with the CEO and Executive Leadership Team to shape the future of one of the region's most dynamic consumer businesses. Reporting directly to the CEO, you will lead the financial strategy and performance of the Australia and New Zealand business, playing a critical role in driving growth, transformation and enterprise-wide decision-making.

Operating within a FTSE-listed global organisation, you will lead an integrated ANZ finance function while shaping the commercial direction of the business. This is a contemporary CFO portfolio that extends well beyond financial stewardship, encompassing enterprise-wide strategy, transformation, commercial performance and organisational capability. Working closely with the Executive Leadership Team, you will provide insight, influence and leadership that enables confident decision-making, drives sustainable growth and delivers long-term value across the business.

Success in this role requires an executive who looks beyond the numbers. You are a commercially astute leader who challenges the status quo, influences at the highest levels and brings financial insight to strategic decision-making. You thrive in fast-paced, complex environments and can balance long-term vision with disciplined execution. Equally comfortable in the boardroom and with your leadership team, you build high-performing cultures that embrace accountability, innovation and change.

You will bring significant senior finance leadership experience, ideally at CFO or Deputy CFO level, within a large, complex, global organisation. You have successfully led strategy, transformation, M&A and enterprise-wide commercial initiatives, with a proven ability to influence executive stakeholders and lead high-performing teams. CA, CPA or an equivalent professional qualification is essential. Experience in digital, technology, consumer or other fast-paced industries will be highly regarded.

This is a rare opportunity to join a global market leader during a period of significant growth and transformation. With broad commercial accountability and genuine influence over strategy and performance, this is a career-defining executive role for an ambitious and forward-thinking finance leader.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Gemma Ledbury on 0423 322 462 or email gemmaledbury@attunedtalent.com.au

job.title: Learning & Development Program Lead
job.description:
This is a rare opportunity for a senior Learning and Development leader who wants to build, shape and own a nationally significant program in an organisation that operates with the pace, autonomy and ambition of a scale-up. Working in a small, purpose-driven team, you will have real influence, the freedom to innovate and the ability to move ideas quickly from concept to delivery.

Leading an end-to-end professional development program that plays a critical role in lifting capability, compliance and performance across industry, you will set the learning strategy and design and embed competency frameworks that ensure all content is practical, engaging and aligned with regulatory and industry expectations. Your focus will be on high-quality adult learning, effective digital delivery and outcomes that are clearly measurable and demonstrable.

You will oversee course design, quality assurance and provider performance, ensuring learning remains current, accessible and audit-ready in a highly regulated environment. Working closely with data, compliance and engagement teams, you will actively use insights from learner behaviour, performance data and regulatory trends to continuously improve the program, proactively address emerging risks and strengthen overall industry outcomes.

Strong commercial judgement and stakeholder capability are critical. You will build and manage partnerships across industry, regulators and commercial organisations to fund content development and support innovation, while maintaining clear guardrails around independence, integrity and compliance.

This opportunity will suit someone who is energised by ambiguity, confident making decisions without perfect information, and motivated by delivery rather than bureaucracy. You enjoy working at pace, influencing through expertise rather than hierarchy, and balancing rigour with pragmatism in a lean, fast-moving environment.

If you are seeking a role where you can genuinely shape direction, see the impact of your work quickly, and be part of an organisation that feels far more like a scale-up than a traditional institution, this role offers a rewarding next step.

job.title: Head of HR Business Partnering
job.description:
Do What’s Right: Win, but not at all costs
Entain is a global leader in sports betting, gaming and interactive entertainment, operating across 40+ regulated markets worldwide. In Australia and New Zealand, Entain represents some of the region’s most recognised brands and is entering a new chapter of organisational evolution.

Following the appointment of a new People Director ANZ , the People function is being reimagined to strengthen strategic alignment, performance outcomes and leadership impact. This newly created Lead HR Business Partner role is central to that evolution.

Keep It Simple: Re-imagine Business Partnering
Reporting to the People Director ANZ, you will play a critical role in shaping and embedding a best-practice business partnering model across the region.

You will:
  • Act as a true strategic partner to senior leaders – aligning people strategy with commercial priorities.
  • Lead and develop a team of HR Business Partners, setting standards of excellence, clarity and accountability.
  • Establish and embed a clear partnering framework – defining “what great looks like” in how HR supports, challenges and enables leaders.
  • Navigate complex, regulated environments with sound judgement and pragmatism.
  • Partner effectively with global Centres of Expertise (Talent, Reward, OD and Resourcing) to deliver locally relevant, globally aligned solutions.
  • Drive workforce planning, organisational design and leadership capability initiatives that enable sustainable performance.

Win Together: Connect Globally, Deliver Locally
We are seeking a commercially sharp and values-aligned HR leader who brings:
  • 10+ years’ HR Business Partnering experience, operating as a trusted advisor to senior leaders.
  • Proven experience leading and coaching a team of HR Business Partners.
  • Exposure to regulated environments (highly regarded), ideally within a technology-enabled or digital workforce.
  • Experience working in a multinational matrix environment, partnering with global Centres of Expertise.
  • A strong work ethic, pragmatic thinking and a proactive, solutions-focused mindset.
  • The ability to navigate complexity, influence outcomes and challenge constructively.
  • Alignment to Entain’s purpose and values – delivering performance, responsibly.
This role will suit a confident, credible HR leader who thrives in pace, brings intellectual rigour and is energised by building frameworks, capability and clarity in partnership with the business.

Why Join Entain ANZ?
This is an opportunity to shape the next phase of HR evolution in ANZ – influencing how leaders are supported, how performance is enabled, and how a high-performing culture is sustained within a global, compliance-led organisation.

A competitive remuneration package is on offer, with Brisbane as the ANZ headquarters.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
Queensland Farmers’ Federation (QFF) is the united voice of Queensland agriculture, representing the interests of peak body members, Queensland agriculture more broadly and regional communities across the state. As the peak body for Queensland’s agricultural sector, QFF advocates on the issues that matter most to industry, government and the future sustainability of farming in Queensland.

Reporting directly to the President and Board, the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will lead the organisation through its next phase of strategic delivery, advocacy and commercial sustainability. Leading a team of approximately 25 staff, the CEO will balance high-level strategic leadership with operational execution, ensuring QFF remains influential, financially sustainable, member-focused and highly regarded across industry and government.

This is a broad and hands-on executive leadership role requiring a commercially astute and politically aware leader who can operate effectively in a fast-paced, stakeholder-driven environment and deliver on peak body members priorities. The CEO will lead the implementation of QFF’s Strategic Plan, oversee organisational performance and financial management, and continue to strengthen relationships across member organisations, government, industry, media and corporate partners.

The successful candidate will bring strong commercial and financial capability, including experience managing budgets, cashflow, grants, partnerships and diversified revenue streams. Equally important will be the ability to lead people, build alignment across competing priorities and represent QFF with credibility, influence and executive presence.
You may currently be leading within a member-based organisation, industry association, government, agribusiness or a complex stakeholder environment where advocacy, commerciality and relationship management are critical to success. An understanding of agriculture and the issues impacting the sector will be highly regarded.
This is a rare opportunity to lead one of Queensland’s most influential industry organisations and play a key role in shaping the future of agriculture across the state.
For an information pack or confidential discussion please contact Gemma Ledbury at gemmaledbury@attunedtalent.com.au

job.title: HR Coordinator
job.description:
We're partnering with a well-established Australian organisation operating across a large, geographically dispersed workforce in a complex heavy industry environment. Supporting operations across multiple regional and remote sites, the business is recognised for its commitment to safety, operational excellence and continuous improvement. The business is now looking for a HR Coordinator who will play a pivotal role in supporting People & Culture operations across a diverse national workforce.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a collaborative and values-driven team where you'll gain exposure to the full employee lifecycle, work with modern HR systems, and contribute to projects focused on continuous improvement and operational excellence.

About the Role

Reporting to a Senior HRBP, you'll be responsible for coordinating end-to-end HR administration from onboarding through to offboarding, while ensuring employee records, workforce data and HR systems remain accurate, compliant and up to date. You'll become a key point of contact for employees and leaders, supporting HR processes and helping deliver an exceptional employee experience.

You'll also have the opportunity to:
 
  • Coordinate employee lifecycle activities including onboarding, employment changes and terminations.
  • Maintain HRIS and workforce data with a strong focus on accuracy and compliance.
  • Support payroll through accurate people data and reporting.
  • Assist with visa and work rights administration.
  • Contribute to HR systems enhancements, process improvements and documentation.
  • Prepare workforce reporting and assist with audits and compliance activities.
  • Partner with stakeholders across the business to provide responsive HR support.


About You
You'll be someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys working with systems and data, and takes pride in delivering exceptional service.

You'll ideally bring:
 
  • Previous experience in an HR Coordinator, HR Administrator or People Operations role.
  • Strong organisational skills with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Confidence using HRIS platforms (Workday experience highly regarded).
  • Experience maintaining confidential employee records and workforce data.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining accuracy.
  • A proactive mindset with a genuine passion for improving processes.

We welcome applications from recent Human Resources graduates who are ready to kick-start their career within a large, complex organisation. This is a fantastic opportunity to gain exposure to the full employee lifecycle, develop your technical HR knowledge and build your experience alongside an experienced and supportive People & Culture team.

What's on Offer?
 
  • Join a collaborative and supportive People & Culture team.
  • Broad exposure across HR operations and employee lifecycle activities.
  • Opportunity to work with contemporary HR systems and contribute to process improvement initiatives.
  • A role where your ideas and attention to detail will genuinely make an impact.
  • Ongoing professional development within a stable and growing organisation.

If you're looking to build your career within a high-performing HR team and enjoy balancing administration, systems, compliance and stakeholder support, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Board Director Opportunities
job.description:
Queensland Domestic and Family Violence Alliance (QDFVA) is the new independent statewide peak body representing specialist domestic and family violence and women’s health services. Working alongside members, government and key stakeholders, QDFVA advocates for system reform, strengthens sector capability and champions evidence-informed responses that improve outcomes for victim-survivors across Queensland.

Guided by the Board Composition Matrix, the Board is looking to appoint three new Non-Executive Directors who will complement the existing skills of the Board and CEO while strengthening QDFVA's strategic capability. This is an opportunity to influence statewide reform, contribute to stronger outcomes for victim-survivors and support the long-term sustainability of Queensland's peak body for specialist domestic and family violence services. Directors will work alongside an experienced Board and leadership team committed to collaboration, integrity and meaningful systems change.

The Opportunities

Research, Data and Evidence
A recognised leader from academia, research or industry with expertise in research, evaluation, data analytics or evidence translation. You will help ensure QDFVA's advocacy, policy positions and strategic decisions are informed by contemporary evidence and emerging research.

Profile Building, Reputation and Strategic Networks
A highly respected senior leader with the influence, networks and credibility to elevate QDFVA's profile across government, business and the broader community. Experience building organisational reputation, opening strategic partnerships and  developing alternate revenue streams including philanthropy will be highly regarded. This role complements existing management capability and is focused on strategic influence, reputation and relationship-building.

First Nations Influence.
This identified position recognises the importance of First Nations leadership and self-determination in shaping policy, governance and sector reform.

About You
We are seeking experienced leaders who can contribute at Board level through strategic thinking, sound governance and collaborative decision-making. You will bring executive, governance or sector leadership experience and a commitment to QDFVA's purpose. Experience in not-for-profit governance is desirable but not essential.

Previous Board experience, director education and a mature understanding of governance, risk and fiduciary responsibilities will be highly regarded.

Applications
Please reach out to Nicola Flannery at nicolaflannery@attunedtalent.com.au for an information pack or call 0416 267 723 for a confidential discussion.

Applications close: Sunday 30th August 2026

job.title: Procurement Lead
job.description:
Our client is a values-driven regional organisation committed to creating thriving, connected communities through the delivery of essential services, sustainable growth and long-term planning. Serving one of Southeast Queensland's most rapidly evolving regions, the organisation works closely with residents, businesses and community stakeholders to balance economic development with the protection of its unique natural environment and lifestyle.

Due to a period of leave, an exciting opportunity has become available for an experienced procurement professional to join the organisation for the next 3-6 months, and lead a small team while driving strategic procurement initiatives, strengthening governance frameworks, and partnering with stakeholders across the organisation to deliver commercial and value-for-money outcomes.

About the Role
This is a role for someone who enjoys balancing strategy with operational delivery. You will have the opportunity to influence procurement practices across the business, improve systems and processes, develop capability within operational teams, and build strong supplier partnerships that support long-term organisational success.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading the end-to-end procurement and contract management function.
  • Managing and mentoring a small procurement team.
  • Reviewing and enhancing procurement policies, frameworks and governance.
  • Providing expert procurement advice to senior leaders and key stakeholders.
  • Leading tender and sourcing activities while ensuring legislative compliance.
  • Driving category management initiatives, supplier performance and commercial outcomes.
  • Identifying opportunities for continuous improvement and implementing more efficient procurement processes.
  • Delivering procurement training and building capability across the organisation.
About You
To be successful, you will bring:
  • Demonstrated experience in strategic procurement, contract management and category management.
  • Strong knowledge of procurement legislation, governance and best practice frameworks.
  • The ability to influence, negotiate and build trusted relationships with stakeholders at all levels.
  • Experience leading tender processes and delivering commercially sound procurement outcomes.
  • Excellent written communication skills and experience preparing procurement documentation.
  • A collaborative leadership style with the ability to coach and develop others.
  • Previous experience within local government or the public sector will be highly regarded but is not essential.
Why Apply?
This is an excellent opportunity to join an organisation that values collaboration, integrity and continuous improvement. You'll have the opportunity to make a lasting impact by modernising procurement practices, leading a capable team, and partnering with leaders across a diverse organisation to deliver meaningful outcomes for the communities it serves.

job.title: HR Consultant
job.description:
Be Brave. Make an Impact.

StreamlineHR believe great HR changes businesses.

For over 12 years, they have partnered with organisations that value trusted advice, practical solutions and genuine relationships. Their consultants become an extension of their clients' leadership teams, supporting businesses through every stage of the employee lifecycle—from everyday people matters to complex strategic projects.

Their clients span construction, engineering, education, community services, health, aged care, professional services and the sporting sector.

The team at StreamlineHR are collaborative, high-performing and genuinely enjoy working together. They trust each other, celebrate success, support one another through challenges and love what they do. This commitment to quality means you get to partner with team members on client work. Their business development strategy is to do great work that people talk about, resulting in a strong referral network and no awkward networking events.

Be Curious. Embrace Variety.

No two days are the same.

In joining StreamlineHR as their next consultant, you'll manage your own portfolio of retained and project-based clients, becoming a trusted adviser to business owners, CEOs, executive teams and Boards. One day you might be coaching leaders, facilitating a CEO performance review or navigating a complex employee relations matter. The next, you could be delivering an organisational review, leading a workplace investigation, developing HR frameworks or supporting a critical recruitment assignment.

You'll work across organisations typically employing between 20 and 200 people, partnering closely with leaders to solve meaningful business challenges. While you'll have the support of a shared Executive Assistant for coordination and administration, you'll need to be comfortable to do the less glamorous grunt work too. This is not a hierarchical business - so whilst you can lean on specialists in the team you’ll be responsible for the delivery to your clients.

Be Kind. Be Authentic. Be You.
We're looking for someone who genuinely loves HR and enjoys building lasting relationships.

You may be an experienced HR leader, or perhaps you're a Senior HR Business Partner ready to step into consulting. Previous consulting experience is advantageous, but what matters most is your ability to combine commercial thinking with practical HR advice and exceptional client care.

You'll be someone who:
  • Builds credibility quickly with senior stakeholders.
  • Is equally comfortable discussing strategy and rolling up your sleeves to get things done.
  • Thrives in a fast-paced, client-focused environment.
  • Enjoys variety, embraces new challenges and isn't easily rattled.
  • Brings warmth, humility, humour and a genuine desire to help others succeed.
If you're looking for a role where you'll work with great clients, exceptional colleagues and make a tangible impact every day, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Sales Coordinator
job.description:
With national operations, our client is a fast-paced ever-evolving business that’s built on innovation, strong values and a friendly and supportive culture. They are focussed on building long-lasting partnerships across the transport and logistics industry, and pride themselves on a commitment to great customer experience. Due to significant growth, they are now seeking an enthusiastic Sales Support Coordinator who will be a valued cornerstone of the Sales and Operations team.

In this pivotal role, you'll play an essential part in all sales and branch operations and work as part of a national team coordinating logistics and maintenance. This role ensures seamless day-to-day operations, administrative excellence, and engagement with a wide range of potential clients.
Your role will include:
  • Direct engagement with current and potential clients
  • Keeping CRM records accurate and up to date
  • Scheduling of service and repairs for vehicles
  • Coordinating with suppliers and assisting with purchasing

About you
This role will suit a university graduate/current student or someone looking to take their first step into a corporate role where you can engage with all aspects of a business and drive success.
To be successful in this role you will have:
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills that set you apart
  • A natural flair for delivering outstanding customer service
  • Superb organisational and time management abilities
  • Strong attention to detail & the ability to problem solve
  • A passion for systems and utilising leading edge technology.



What they offer:
  • A robust internal training program to set you up for success
  • Competitive base salary with incremental increases at 6 months & 12 months
  • Commission eligibility above market rate
  • Potential career progression into Management roles
